rationale: The deflator swap is defensible on a real mechanical ground (net-operating-asset denominators can go negative and flip the ratio's sign, while act−che cannot), but it remains a fairly incremental re-scaling of the archive's best signal rather than a new mechanism, and act−che near zero for asset-light or financial firms will still create tail instability that 1% winsorization only partly tames.

This is essentially the sign flip of the already-tested LiabilityStretchGradedProfit (whose −4.1% alpha at t=−2.7 mechanically implies roughly +4% here), so the "result" is pre-determined by archive information rather than tested, and the underlying content — liability-side accruals carrying the conventional Sloan sign — is a direct restatement of the published accrual anomaly.

This is a rescaling of GrossProfitGradedByBloat rather than a new mechanism, and its stated logic is internally inconsistent: it claims to hold the firm ordering fixed for the FMB regression while simultaneously claiming to neutralize industry composition, which the final IND_RANK cannot do at once since within-industry ranking necessarily changes the cross-sectional ordering the decile portfolios saw.

The book-tax conformity channel is genuinely absent from the archive and the pretax-income leg is correctly matched to the tax accrual, but txp is a balance-sheet payable — a high stock can equally mean deferred cash outflow, which is a liability-side accrual with the opposite (Sloan) sign — so the mechanism is ambiguous and txp's sparse, lumpy reporting is a real coverage/noise risk.

A one-year change in gross-profit-to-working-capital is close to the long-published Abarbanell-Bushee / Piotroski fundamental signals on changes in margin and asset turnover, it abandons the cross-theme interaction mandate entirely (it is a single-ratio delta), and differencing a ratio with a small, volatile denominator will be dominated by denominator noise.

Benchmarking non-cash working-capital growth against sales growth is a substantively different normalization from the asset-deflated conditioners already tested, the sign logic is internally coherent, and it plausibly separates genuine expansion from accrual inflation — though it overlaps conceptually with Jones-model abnormal accruals, so the novelty rests on the profitability interaction and on growth-rate stability for small-denominator firms.
